arxiv-1901-08053.title: Quantum States of a Time-Asymmetric Universe: Wave Function, Density Matrix, and Empirical Equivalence
arxiv-1901-08053.creator: Eddy Keming Chen
arxiv-1901-08053.description: Abstract What is the quantum state of the universe? Although there have been several interesting suggestions, the question remains open. In this paper, I consider a natural choice for the universal quantum state arising from the Past Hypothesis, a boundary condition that accounts for the time-asymmetry of the universe.

arxiv-1907-08657.title: Learning More From Less Conference: Proceedings of the 42nd International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 21–25, 2019; Paris, France Proceedings of the 42nd International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR
arxiv-1907-08657.creator: Dany Haddad, Joydeep Ghosh
arxiv-1907-08657.description: Abstract . The limited availability of ground truth relevance labels has been a major impediment to the application of supervised methods to ad-hoc retrieval. As a result, unsupervised scoring methods, such as BM25, remain strong competitors to deep learning techniques which have brought on dramatic improvements in other domains, such as computer vision and natural language processing.

arxiv-2210-10131.title: Symmetric homology is representation homology
arxiv-2210-10131.creator: Yuri Berest, Ajay C. Ramadoss
arxiv-2210-10131.description: Abstract . Symmetric homology is a natural generalization of cyclic homology, in which symmetric groups play the role of cyclic groups. In the case of associative algebras, the symmetric homology theory was introduced by Z. Fiedorowicz [ 19 ] and was further developed in the work of S. Ault [ 1 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2305-02672.title: Proving Properties of φ \varphi -Representations with the Walnut Theorem-Prover
arxiv-2305-02672.creator: Jeffrey Shallit
arxiv-2305-02672.description: Abstract We revisit a classic theorem of Frougny and Sakarovitch concerning automata for φ \varphi -representations, and show how to obtain it in a different and more computationally direct way. Using it, we can find simple, induction-free proofs of existing results in the literature about these representations, in a uniform and straightforward manner.

arxiv-2405-11598.title: AI-Assisted Diagnosis for Covid-19 CXR Screening: From Data Collection to Clinical Validation
arxiv-2405-11598.creator: Carlo Alberto Barbano 1,2 \sthanks Correspondence: carlo.barbano@unito.it Riccardo Renzulli 1 Marco Grosso 3 Domenico Basile 3 Marco Busso 3 Marco Grangetto 1
arxiv-2405-11598.description: Abstract In this paper, we present the major results from the Covid Radiographic imaging System based on AI (Co.R.S.A.) project, which took place in Italy. This project aims to develop a state-of-the-art AI-based system for diagnosing Covid-19 pneumonia from Chest X-ray (CXR) images.

arxiv-2505-02436.title: Jet shape modification in a transport calculation
arxiv-2505-02436.creator: Monideepa Maity, Subrata Pal
arxiv-2505-02436.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Monideepa Maity, Subrata Pal. A precise quantification of the medium-modification of the high transverse momenta jets in relativistic heavy ion collisions rely on consistent modeling of elastic and inelastic energy loss suffered by the jet and the concurrent underlying medium evolution. We have developed a unified framework for jet and bulk medium evolution within a multiphase transport approach where the jets and medium share energy and momentum via multiple elastic scatterings and medium-induced gluon radiation during the parton transport.

pmc-10635344.creator: Kelley A. Jones, Amy G. Clark, Melissa A. Greiner, Emma Sandoe, Abhigya Giri, Bradley G. Hammill, Courtney H. Van Houtven, Aparna Higgins, Brystana Kaufman

pmc-12427404.title: Pulmonary Carcinoids: Diagnostic and Therapeutic Approach
pmc-12427404.creator: Francesco Petrella, Andrea Cara, Enrico Mario Cassina, Lidia Libretti, Emanuele Pirondini, Federico Raveglia, Maria Chiara Sibilia, Antonio Tuoro, Stefania Rizzo, Paul Jules van Houtte
pmc-12427404.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryPulmonary carcinoid tumors are a rare type of lung cancer, making up about 1–2% of all lung cancers. However, they account for about a quarter to a third of all slow-growing neuroendocrine tumors. While these tumors are uncommon in adults, they are actually the most common form of lung cancer found in children and teenagers, with the typical carcinoid being the most frequent type.

pmc-12528745.title: Efficient hybrid fuzzy weighted 3D FCNN with TSO PSO optimization for accurate multi modal MRI brain tumor classification
pmc-12528745.creator: Liu Feng, Guo Hao, Wang Jian
pmc-12528745.description: Detecting and segmenting brain tumors from 3D MRI images is a challenging and time-intensive task for clinicians. This research introduces an innovative hybrid architecture for deep learning, comprising a 3D fully convolutional neural network (3D-FCNN), an interval type-2 fuzzy weighting system, and a hybrid transit search optimization-particle swarm optimization (Hybrid-TSO-PSO) algorithm.

pmc-12541670.title: Trematode Infection Prevalence Increases With Snail Richness: Observations From a 4‐Year Study of Snail–Trematode Interactions
pmc-12541670.creator: Brooke A. McPhail, Carol M. Frost, Simon J. G. Otto, Patrick C. Hanington
pmc-12541670.description: Digenetic trematodes are valuable study organisms for exploring how biodiversity influences disease. In this study, we investigated the relationship between snail richness and trematode infection prevalence using data from a 4‐year study (2019–2022) of eight wetland sites in Alberta, Canada.

pmc-12577983.title: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy: a rare case report highlighting seizure presentation in a 27-year-old female
pmc-12577983.creator: Mohammad Obada Alsadi, John Latifa, Dani Alokla, Mohamad Ismaeel Darkaznli, Lulyah Al Almallah, Fatema Channan, Momen Jamal AlSalloum Alibrahim
pmc-12577983.description: Introduction:Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TC) is a transient form of left ventricular dysfunction often triggered by emotional or physical stress. It mimics acute myocardial infarction but occurs without obstructive coronary artery disease. The exact pathophysiology remains unclear, though excessive catecholamine release is believed to play a role.

pmc-12663688.title: Anisakid larvae in the organs of Atlantic mackerel, Scomber scombrus (L.): Host or parasite superiority?
pmc-12663688.creator: Bahram Sayyaf Dezfuli, Giovanni Bernacchia, Morena De Bastiani, Martina Pinca, Emanuela Franchella, Luca Bellini, Giuseppe Castaldelli, Luisa Giari
pmc-12663688.description: Members of the Anisakidae family, in particular the genus Anisakis are among the most common seafood-borne parasites which may lead to anisakidosis, a zoonotic disease. Anisakis simplex (s.s.) (Rudolphi, 1809) can infect humans by means of the ingestion of raw or undercooked fish harbouring the third-stage larvae of this nematode.

pmc-12668717.title: Cerebral Oxygenation Pattern during Therapeutic Hypothermia after Perinatal Asphyxia: A Single Center Cohort Study
pmc-12668717.creator: Thomas Alderliesten, Corline E.J. Parmentier, Manon J.N.L. Benders, Linda S. de Vries, Daniel C. Vijlbrief, Jeroen Dudink, Maria-Luisa Tataranno, Petra M.A. Lemmers, Floris Groenendaal, Frank van Bel
pmc-12668717.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionInvestigation the association between cerebral oxygenation and short-term adverse outcome in asphyxiated infants with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) during therapeutic hypothermia (TH).MethodsNear infrared spectroscopic-derived cerebral oxygen saturation (rScO2) pattern during first 4 days was compared to early brain MRI (4–10 days) using the Weeke score to define MRI-derived brain injury of infants with GA >35 weeks treated with TH within 6 h between 2010 and 2023. Weeke scores of >9 were considered adverse short-term outcome.

pmc-12993295.title: Biological Performance of Modified Glass Ionomer Cement: Antibacterial Activity, Cytocompatibility, and Rabbit Pulpal Response
pmc-12993295.creator: Krittee Dejyong, Saowakon Indoung, Peerapon Sornying, Sareepah Manmoo, Nattapon Rotpenpian
pmc-12993295.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundConventional glass ionomer cement (GIC) is widely used as a restorative base and liner owing to its chemical adhesion to dentine, fluoride release, and favourable biocompatibility. Nevertheless, its intrinsic antibacterial activity and regenerative capacity remain limited. To enhance these properties, a series of modified GIC formulations, referred to as BIOGIC, incorporating tricalcium phosphate (TCP), TCTP-derived peptides, and 10% chlorhexidine (CHX), were developed.

pmc-13065771.title: Probabilistic day-ahead forecasting of system-level renewable energy and electricity demand
pmc-13065771.creator: Guillermo Terrén-Serrano, Ranjit Deshmukh, Manel Martínez-Ramón
pmc-13065771.description: Increasing shares of wind and solar generation, together with rising electricity demand, introduce growing uncertainty into power system operations. Accurate day-ahead forecasts of electricity demand and renewable generation are essential for system operators to coordinate electricity markets and maintain reliability at low cost.

pmc-13081319.title: Development of an automated chemiluminescence immunoassay for detection of IgA antibodies against porcine epidemic diarrhea virus spike
pmc-13081319.creator: Duan Li, Daoping Zeng, Qi Wang, Leyi Zhang, Yanling Liu, Cuiqin Huang, Changxu Song, Lei Wang
pmc-13081319.description: BackgroundPorcine epidemic diarrhoea virus (PEDV) causes substantial financial losses on pig farming worldwide. Monitoring PEDV-specific IgA antibodies is essential for assessing vaccine efficacy. In this study, we developed a fully automated chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) for the detection of PEDV IgA antibodies in both serum and milk.

pmc-13221265.title: The Omentum as a Lymphoid Tissue: Its Molecular Aspects and Application in a Murine Model
pmc-13221265.creator: Masahiro Hojo, Dongkyung Seo, Riri Ito, Kosuke Ishikawa, Takahiro Miura, Emi Funayama, Yuhei Yamamoto, Taku Maeda
pmc-13221265.description: BackgroundThe omentum is a vascularized, immune-active tissue with regenerative potential, particularly when activated by intraperitoneal stimuli. Its secreted factors may promote lymphangiogenesis, offering a novel approach to lymphedema treatment.Methods The omentum was activated in mice using an intraperitoneal polydextran slurry. Gene expression was evaluated over time to assess inflammatory and lymphatic markers.

pmc-13226659.title: Antibiotic-induced gut microbiome dysbiosis: risks and strategies for mitigation
pmc-13226659.creator: Katharina Müller, Justine Gillard, Athanasios Typas, Michael Knopp, Camille V Goemans
pmc-13226659.description: The discovery of antibiotics and their subsequent therapeutic use revolutionized our ability to treat once deadly infectious diseases, and antibiotics have become one of the most commonly prescribed drug classes. Unfortunately, these compounds not only target pathogenic strains, but also non-pathogenic bacteria that fulfill important functions for the human host.

pmc-13263977.title: Non-technical skills in the management of endoscopic adverse events
pmc-13263977.creator: Tessa Herman, Mohammad Bilal
pmc-13263977.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Adverse events are an inherent risk of performing endoscopic procedures. Although the rate of serious adverse events during routine endoscopic procedures is relatively low, most gastroenterologists will encounter at least one significant adverse event during their careers. Traditional endoscopic training largely focuses on teaching the technical management of adverse events with less emphasis on the cognitive and interpersonal competencies that are critical to patient safety.

pmc-13523020.title: Nanostructured antimicrobial fertilizers for sustainable agriculture: integrating targeted pathogen suppression with controlled nutrient release and enhanced crop productivity
pmc-13523020.creator: Sanduni Dabare, Imalka Munaweera
pmc-13523020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The agricultural sector is facing greater challenges than ever to increase crop productivity while reducing chemical use and environmental impacts. By incorporating targeted pathogen suppression with controlled nutrient release mechanisms, nanostructured antimicrobial fertilizers can address these complex challenges. The information available on the development, characterization and application of nanostructured fertilizers with antimicrobial agents such as metal oxide nanoparticles (ZnO, CuO, and TiO2), silver nanoparticles and bioactive compounds is summarized in the present review.
